{
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "title": "1. Unequal protein maturation or assay conditions produce an apparent species difference",
      "question_and_explanation": "Does the reported activity gap reflect unequal amounts of properly folded, processed, zinc-containing ADA2 rather than different intrinsic chemistry? CTX-01 reports lower pig activity without assay conditions or an effect size. Signal-peptide and glycosylation annotations differ between species, but actual recombinant processing is unknown (CTX-03). Preparation-dependent changes could affect secretion, stability or dimer assembly. If this explanation is correct, pig ADA2 may retain substantial free-adenosine activity when comparably prepared; preservation of DNA-related functions would still require separate testing.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": [
        "CTX-01",
        "CTX-02",
        "CTX-03",
        "CTX-06"
      ],
      "conflicting_evidence_ids": [],
      "evidence_notes": "These records establish unresolved preparation variables, not a demonstrated preparation defect. CTX-02 establishes zinc involvement and human dimerization, not pig zinc occupancy or assembly. The pig reference sequence may not match the experimental construct (CTX-06). No supplied observation directly contradicts this hypothesis.",
      "alternative_explanation": "Correctly matured pig ADA2 has intrinsically weaker free-adenosine catalysis because of sequence-dependent differences in substrate recognition or catalytic dynamics.",
      "proposed_test": "First verify the experimental construct sequences and reproduce the comparison using independent human and pig preparations made in the same expression system with matched tag handling. Quantify intact mature protein and characterize processing, glycosylation, folding, oligomeric state and zinc content. Measure adenosine-to-inosine initial rates across substrate concentrations and a shared range of assay conditions. If a preparation difference is identified, correct that variable and repeat the activity comparison.",
      "predicted_outcome_if_true": "Activity tracks a preparation or condition variable, and correcting it substantially narrows the species gap. A condition-dependent gap would weaken the claim of universally low pig activity, although it could still reflect an intrinsic difference in condition preference.",
      "falsifying_outcome": "The gap persists across independent preparations and shared conditions despite comparable intact protein amounts, maturation, folding, assembly and zinc content. Failure to rescue activity after correcting an identified defect would weaken that defect as the explanation.",
      "controls_and_feasibility": "Include no-enzyme and mock-purification controls, product standards, independent preparations, and verification of initial-rate linearity with time and protein amount. Use matched treatment controls for any processing or glycan intervention and recheck folding afterward. Protein production and chromatography are supported by CTX-08 and CTX-09; mass-spectrometry cores are available under CTX-10, although access and turnaround are unspecified.",
      "next_decision": "If correction removes the gap, standardize preparations before assigning biological meaning to the original result, then compare DNA-related activities. If the gap persists with adequate quality controls, prioritize intrinsic substrate-selectivity tests. If protein quality remains unequal, resolve that uncertainty before interpreting species-specific kinetics.",
      "added_value_from_computation": "No computational evidence was provided. The preparation-first design comes from the missing information in CTX-01, the processing annotations in CTX-03 and construct uncertainty in CTX-06. Effects of maturation, metal occupancy and folding on measured enzyme activity are general biochemical reasoning, not demonstrated findings for these pig preparations.",
      "confidence": "moderate"
    },
    {
      "title": "2. Pig ADA2 has altered substrate preference while retaining DNA-associated functions",
      "question_and_explanation": "Does pig ADA2 handle free adenosine poorly while retaining DNA binding and possibly DNA-associated deamination? CTX-04 reports ADA2–DNA interactions and conversion of DNA deoxyadenosine to deoxyinosine, motivating a direct comparison with free-substrate activity. Sequence-dependent substrate recognition or access could selectively alter free-adenosine activity without abolishing these other functions. No supplied alignment or pig structure identifies a responsible residue.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": [
        "CTX-01",
        "CTX-02",
        "CTX-04"
      ],
      "conflicting_evidence_ids": [],
      "evidence_notes": "CTX-01 supports only the reported direction of the free-adenosine difference. CTX-04 motivates alternative functional measurements but does not establish any DNA activity in pig ADA2. There is no direct evidence for altered pig substrate preference and no supplied contradictory result.",
      "alternative_explanation": "Pig ADA2 is broadly catalytically impaired rather than substrate-selective. Apparent preservation of DNA activity could instead arise from nonspecific binding, contaminating enzymes, free nucleosides in the DNA preparation or unequal protein quality.",
      "proposed_test": "Using quality-matched preparations, compare concentration-dependent activity on free adenosine, free deoxyadenosine and defined deoxyadenosine-containing DNA. Independently measure DNA binding, deoxyinosine formation within recovered DNA and DNA strand integrity. Including free deoxyadenosine distinguishes a sugar-dependent preference from a preference for DNA context. Assess whether DNA-associated activity is relatively spared compared with the free-adenosine deficit.",
      "predicted_outcome_if_true": "Pig ADA2 shows a reproducibly different substrate-activity profile, with DNA-associated deamination relatively preserved despite weak free-adenosine activity. Preserved binding alone would support retained interaction capacity, but not preserved DNA editing or the full substrate-selectivity hypothesis.",
      "falsifying_outcome": "All catalytic activities fall proportionately after protein-quality normalization, supporting general impairment rather than altered substrate preference. Failure to detect pig DNA binding or DNA-associated deamination while the human controls work would contradict preservation of the corresponding function. A signal confined to free nucleosides would not establish DNA editing.",
      "controls_and_feasibility": "Include human ADA2, no-enzyme, mock-purification and substrate-only controls; independent protein batches; nucleic-acid competition controls for binding; and confirmation that substrate DNA lacks free nucleosides. Separate DNA-associated products from soluble products and assess strand integrity independently: binding, editing and cutting are not interchangeable. Control protein amount, folding, processing, glycans, assembly, zinc and assay conditions. Chromatography and mass-spectrometry access support feasibility (CTX-09, CTX-10), but assay development and core availability remain unspecified.",
      "next_decision": "If DNA editing is relatively spared, pursue verified sequence alignment and substrate-recognition candidates before designing substitutions. If only binding is preserved, prioritize noncatalytic interaction studies. If neither is preserved, investigate general catalytic impairment. Following biochemical evidence of preservation, test pig versus human rescue of DNA-associated localization or TLR9 responses in an ADA2-deficient cellular system, controlling protein uptake and abundance; biochemical preservation alone does not establish cellular rescue.",
      "added_value_from_computation": "No computational evidence was provided. CTX-04 changes the experiment from an adenosine-only assay to separate binding, DNA-editing and strand-integrity measurements. The free-deoxyadenosine comparator and substrate-recognition mechanism are general biochemical reasoning. CTX-08 supports later localization work, but the existing ADA2 aptamer's recognition of pig ADA2 must be validated rather than assumed.",
      "confidence": "low"
    }
  ],
  "overall_note": "Prioritize matched-preparation replication, then the substrate-panel experiment. All literature observations are supplied as drafts requiring verification; the activity difference lacks an effect size and assay details. Two hypotheses are proposed because no computational evidence supports residue-specific mechanisms. Similar inflammatory disease in ADA2-deficient pigs (CTX-07) motivates functional comparison but does not identify which molecular activity is preserved."
}
